column1: # THE ALDENHAM HAWKINS BAPTISM REGISTER, READ ENTIRE — AND JOHN b.1820 HAS PARENTS.
# Findmypast, Hertfordshire Baptisms, surname HAWKINS at ALDENHAM: 141 entries, every page read.
# Work list row 128. Read 12 October 2026, inside the subscription window.
# WHY. Row 128 wanted the parents of JOHN HAWKINS b.1820 and EMMA b.1822, the couple at THE RED LION
# COTTAGES, Aldenham, in 1871 — Derrick's great-great-grandparents through Emma's daughter Emma, who
# married Robert Wear at Southwark in 1881. The row proposed the 1841 and 1851 censuses. THE 1841
# CENSUS CANNOT ANSWER IT, and that is the first finding below.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT THE 1841 CENSUS ACTUALLY SHOWS, WHICH IS NOT WHAT THE ROW EXPECTED ----------------

column6: *** AT TWENTY HE WAS ALREADY OUT OF THE FAMILY HOME, SO 1841 GIVES NO PARENTS. *** All twenty Hawkins entries for Aldenham in 1841 were read. Three Johns: b.1811 (30, heading his own family with Ann at Reservoir), b.1826 (15, son of Jeremiah and Elizabeth at a Cottage) and b.1821 (20) — and the twenty-year-old is BOARDING AT ALDENHAM CHECKERS in a household of three with KATHERINE NICHOLLS, 70, and WILLIAM KIMPTON, 20. HO107/438/3 folio 7 page 8 schedule 438. No parents in it. Remember 1841 rounds ages 15 and over DOWN to the nearest five, so "20" means 20 to 24.

column1: # ---------------- SO THE BAPTISM REGISTER WAS READ INSTEAD, AND IT ANSWERS ----------------

column6: *** THE ONLY JOHN HAWKINS BAPTISED AT ALDENHAM IN THE WHOLE WINDOW, AND THE OTHERS ARE EXCLUDED BY AGE. *** The register's other Johns are 1824 (Jeremiah and Elizabeth), 1826 (George and Ann), 1598, 1856, 1857, 1861 and 1875 — none of them can be a man of 51 in 1871. A baptism in 1819 fits a birth in 1819 or 1820 exactly. NOT PROOF AND SAID SO: the register cannot show that this child is the Red Lion man. It is the only candidate it allows, with the rest ruled out on age.

# after Robert, which is what a household looks like when the older children have gone to service or
# married. NO CLAIM IS MADE ABOUT WHERE THEY WENT.
# ---------------- AND THE SAME AFTERNOON, EMMA'S HALF CLOSED TOO ----------------

column6: *** SHE IS EMMA LARKIN, AND HER PARENTS ARE ROBERT AND MARY LARKIN. *** Baptised at Aldenham in 1822, birth year given as 1822 — which is EXACTLY the year the 1871 census gives Emma Hawkins, wife, 49, born Aldenham. She is the only Emma Larkin baptised at Aldenham in that generation; the other two in the set are 1869 and 1900. NOT PROOF, SAID PLAINLY: a baptism cannot show this child became the Red Lion wife. It is the only candidate the register allows and the birth year matches to the year.

*** THE ROUTE WAS THE BANNS, NOT THE GRO INDEX. *** Hertfordshire Banns & Marriages, Aldenham: "JOHN HAWKINS — Banns date 18 SEPTEMBER 1842 — Spouse EMMA LARKIN — groom's residence ALDENHAM, bride's residence ALDENHAM." The only John-and-Emma pair in all 44 Hawkins marriage entries for the parish, and it falls exactly where Robert's 1843 baptism said it must. THE PARISH REGISTER ANSWERED WHAT THE GRO INDEX WOULD ONLY HAVE HINTED AT: this archive has refused MarriageFinder's page-mate suggestions three times, and here the register simply names her.

*** AND THE RECORD IS A BANNS ENTRY, WHICH IS NOT A MARRIAGE. *** Its "Marriage year" field is EMPTY. Banns are the announcement on three Sundays; the wedding usually follows within weeks and sometimes does not happen at all. THE MARRIAGE ITSELF HAS NOT BEEN SEEN. What makes it near-certain rather than merely likely is the baptism of ROBERT HAWKINS to John and Emma at the same parish the following year.

AND THE NAMING PATTERN CORROBORATES WITHOUT BEING ASKED, which is worth one line and no more: their ELDEST SON IS ROBERT, 1843 — Emma's father's name — and they have a MARY, 1861, which is the name of BOTH grandmothers. That is a convention of the period and not evidence; it is recorded because it agrees rather than because it proves.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT IS STILL OPEN, SO NOBODY THINKS THIS ROW IS DONE ----------------

column6: THE LARKINS THEMSELVES ARE UNREAD. Robert and Mary Larkin of Aldenham have not been looked for in any census or register, and Emma's siblings are unknown. The same method would do it: the parish is small and the surname is rare there.

SUPERSEDED BY THE ROW ABOVE — her maiden name WAS unknown and is now LARKIN. Left in place so the shape of the question is still legible: *** THERE IS NO EMMA AMONG THE TWENTY ALDENHAM HAWKINSES OF 1841, *** which was the clue that she was a Hawkins only by marriage, and it was right.

column1: # ---------------- AND A THIRD GENERATION, THE SAME EVENING: BOTH GRANDPARENT COUPLES NAMED ----------------

column6: *** JOHN'S PARENTS MARRIED AT ALDENHAM: WILLIAM HAWKINS AND MARY APPLEYARD, BANNS 20 APRIL 1800, *** both resident in the parish. The only William-and-Mary pair among the 44 Hawkins marriage entries — the other Williams marry a Sarah in 1792, a Sarah in 1825 and a Mary Ann in 1870 — and their first child GEORGE is baptised in 1801, which is where a marriage of April 1800 puts him. *** MARY'S MAIDEN NAME IS APPLEYARD, a surname this archive has never held.

*** EMMA'S PARENTS MARRIED AT ALDENHAM: ROBERT LARKIN AND MARY BURCH, BANNS 16 JANUARY 1814, *** both resident in the parish. All 30 Larkin marriage entries for Aldenham were read and this is the ONLY Robert-and-Mary pair; the other Roberts marry an Elizabeth in 1748 and an Anne in 1774. Emma is baptised to a Robert and a Mary in 1822, eight years after. *** MARY'S MAIDEN NAME IS BURCH, also new to this archive.

SO THE LINE NOW READS, on Derrick's English side: Emma Hawkins b.1859, who married Robert Wear at Southwark in 1881 — daughter of JOHN HAWKINS b.1819 and EMMA LARKIN b.1822 — who are the children of WILLIAM HAWKINS and MARY APPLEYARD, and of ROBERT LARKIN and MARY BURCH, all four of Aldenham. TWO GENERATIONS AND THREE NEW SURNAMES IN ONE AFTERNOON, from a parish register and nothing bought.

*** THE SAME CAVEAT APPLIES TO ALL THREE MARRIAGES AND IS NOT WAIVED BECAUSE IT IS REPETITIVE: EVERY ONE IS A BANNS ENTRY WITH AN EMPTY MARRIAGE-YEAR FIELD. *** Banns are the announcement on three Sundays; the wedding usually follows and is not proved by them. In each case what supports it is a baptism to that couple in the same parish soon after — George 1801, Emma 1822, Robert 1843. AND THE IDENTIFICATIONS ARE BEST-CANDIDATE, NOT PROOF: in each the register offers exactly one pair of the right names in the right window, which is a weaker thing than a document naming the person.

INSTRUMENT: *** THIS SET INDEXES EACH BANNS CALLING SEPARATELY, so one wedding appears two or three times *** under different record ids — the 1800 Hawkins marriage has two entries and one of them says "(the first of three)". COUNTING ENTRIES IS NOT COUNTING MARRIAGES, and a careless reader would make two weddings out of one.

column1: # ---------------- AND HER FATHER'S OWN PARENTS ARE NOT ESTABLISHED, WHICH IS THE HONEST ANSWER ----------------

column6: *** TWO CANDIDATES AND NO WAY HERE TO CHOOSE BETWEEN THEM. *** Robert married Mary Burch by banns in January 1814. The register offers ROBERT LARKIN BAPTISED 1789, son of ROBERT AND ANN — who would be 24 — and ROBERT LARKIN BAPTISED 1781, son of JAMES AND SARAH — who would be 33. BOTH ARE ORDINARY MARRIAGE AGES. Unlike John Hawkins and Emma Larkin, where the register offered exactly one candidate in the window, here it offers two and this archive picks neither.

*** THREE ROUTES TRIED AND ALL THREE CLOSED. *** (1) THE 1841 CENSUS CANNOT DISCRIMINATE: the rounding would separate them — b.1789 recorded as 50, b.1781 as 60 — but THERE IS ONLY ONE ROBERT LARKIN IN ALDENHAM IN 1841 AND HE IS THE SON, aged 20, baptised 1821. Our Robert is absent from the parish: dead before 1841, or moved. (2) BURIALS CANNOT DISCRIMINATE: one Robert Larkin burial exists at Aldenham, 1 SEPTEMBER 1793, AND THE INDEX CARRIES NO AGE, so it cannot be told whether it is the father of the Robert-and-Ann family, the twelve-year-old of 1781, or a third man. (3) And a 1793 burial does not even cleanly orphan the Robert-and-Ann family, whose last two baptisms are Ann 1793 and James born 1794 — a child conceived before a September death is unremarkable.

column1: # ---------------- AND AN INSTRUMENT FAULT THAT PRODUCED A FALSE ZERO IN THIS VERY SEARCH ----------------

column6: *** A FORENAME SEARCH DOES NOT EXPAND ABBREVIATIONS, AND IT FAILS SILENTLY. *** firstname=robert + lastname=larkin + place=aldenham in Hertfordshire Burials returns ZERO. The burial is indexed “ROBT” and the zero is an artefact of the abbreviation, not an absence. IT WAS CAUGHT ONLY BY THE CONTROL: surname LARKIN at Aldenham with no forename returns TEN, and SMITH at Aldenham returns NINETY, so the set covers the parish and holds the surname. THIS GENERALISES A RULE THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HAS: “one spelling is not a search” was earned on SURNAMES, from the Geneteka sweep where LOWINSKI found what LUWINSKI did not. IT APPLIES TO FORENAMES TOO, and the pre-1850 parish registers are full of Robt, Wm, Jas, Danl, Thos, Eliz and Jno — all of which appear in these very results. NEVER SEARCH A FORENAME ALONE IN A PARISH SET; search the surname and read the block.

column1: # ---------------- 13 OCTOBER: THE 1851 CENSUS, AND IT REVISES THE FAMILY IN THREE WAYS ----------------

column6: *** LETCHMORE HEATH, ALDENHAM, 1851 — HO107 piece 1714 folio 19 page 1 schedule 2. *** John Hawkins, HEAD, married, AGRICULTURAL LABOURER, age 39. Emma, WIFE, BIRTH YEAR 1822 — which is Emma Larkin to the year and is what identifies the household. Then WILLIAM b.1841, ROBERT b.1843, JOHN b.1847 and BETSEY b.1849. A hamlet of the parish; by 1871 they are at The Red Lion Cottages.

*** THE ELDEST SON WAS BORN ABOUT A YEAR BEFORE THE BANNS, which were 18 September 1842. *** Stated as a fact about dates and nothing else; it was ordinary, and it is also the likeliest reason the banns were called when they were. HE IS NOT IN THE ALDENHAM BAPTISM REGISTER.

ALSO NOT IN THE ALDENHAM BAPTISM REGISTER — and the register DOES hold a John baptised to John and Emma in 1856, so THE 1856 JOHN IS A SECOND JOHN and this one had most likely died. The same pattern as the two Josephs among Emma's own siblings.

*** SO THE NINE CHILDREN ARE AT LEAST ELEVEN, AND THE CAVEAT WRITTEN YESTERDAY WAS NEEDED WITHIN A DAY. *** That row said the baptism list was NOT CLAIMED AS COMPLETE, because “a child baptised elsewhere, or not baptised, does not appear”. Two such children are now named from the census. A PARISH REGISTER READ ENTIRE IS COMPLETE FOR THAT REGISTER AND NOT FOR THAT FAMILY, which is a different sentence and the one to carry.

*** AND AN EIGHT-YEAR AGE DISCREPANCY ON JOHN HIMSELF, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. *** 1851 gives him 39, so born about 1812; 1871 gives him 51, so born about 1820; the baptism this archive matched him to is 1819. TWO OF THE THREE AGREE and the 1851 age is the outlier. IT DOES NOT OPEN A SECOND CANDIDATE: the Aldenham register holds NO John Hawkins baptised between 1810 and 1814 — its Johns are 1819, 1824 and 1826 — so there is no 1812 baptism for the 1851 age to point at. The 1819 identification stands as the only one the register allows, and the discrepancy is noted because an age in one census is not evidence against a baptism, only against another age.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE FOURTH GENERATION IS OUTSIDE THE COUNTY: BOTH MOTHERS ARE ABSENT ----------------

column6: *** NOT BAPTISED IN HERTFORDSHIRE. *** She married William Hawkins by banns in April 1800, so was born about 1775-1782. ALL 18 APPLEYARD BAPTISMS AT ALDENHAM were read: a John-and-Hannah family ending 1749 and a William-and-Ann family beginning 1809, with NOTHING IN BETWEEN. County-wide, the only Mary Appleyards in the whole set are one child of 1851 at Aldenham, indexed twice.

*** NOT BAPTISED IN HERTFORDSHIRE EITHER. *** She married Robert Larkin by banns in January 1814, so was born about 1790-1796. All 7 Burch baptisms at Aldenham are 1811 or later. County-wide the Marys are 1723 Harpenden, 1737 Bovingdon, and then nothing until 1857 — none within forty years of her window.

THE CONTROL IS ALREADY IN HAND AND IT IS THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN WORK: the Aldenham register is DEMONSTRABLY WELL COVERED for 1770-1800, because today's Larkin and Hawkins sweeps of the same parish returned baptisms at 1772, 1773, 1775, 1777, 1778, 1779, 1781, 1783, 1786, 1789, 1791, 1793 and 1794. The absence of these two women is therefore REAL and not a gap in the register. BOTH MARRIED INTO ALDENHAM FROM OUTSIDE IT. “Of this parish” in a banns entry is a statement of RESIDENCE AT THE TIME, not of birth, and this is the first place in the Aldenham work where that distinction bites.

SO THE METHOD HAS REACHED ITS EDGE. Reading one small parish entire works until somebody marries in from elsewhere; past that point it is a county-wide or national search on a common forename, which is a different and much weaker instrument. RESIDUAL RISK NAMED: the county-wide passes used a FORENAME filter, and this archive learned yesterday that a forename search does not expand abbreviations. For Appleyard the surname-only Aldenham block corroborates the negative; FOR BURCH COUNTY-WIDE IT DOES NOT, and that pass should be redone surname-only before the negative is leaned on.

column1: # ---------------- THE INSTRUMENT, MEASURED, BECAUSE TWO OF THESE COST TIME TODAY ----------------

column6: *** `page=` IS NOT THE PAGINATION PARAMETER AND IT DOES NOT FAIL LOUDLY. *** Adding &page=5 to a Findmypast results URL returns "0 results found" — the parameter is not ignored, it is treated as a filter that nothing matches. THE PAGINATION PARAMETER IS `_page=`, with an underscore. This is the same shape of trap as the year-filter rule already recorded in row 108: A ZERO THAT IS AN ARTEFACT OF THE QUERY AND LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE AN ABSENCE.

AND THE PLACE PARAMETER DIFFERS BY SET. `keywordsplace=aldenham` filters the 1841 census (20 results) and DOES NOT FILTER Hertfordshire Baptisms at all (2,056 — the whole county's Hawkinses). `place=aldenham` filters the baptisms correctly, CONTROLLED BY READING THE PLACE COLUMN OF EVERY ROW RETURNED: all 141 say Aldenham.

the results are ordered BY FORENAME, not by year, so there is no skipping to a date: all ten pages must be read. The set exposes FATHER'S and MOTHER'S FORENAMES in the result row itself, which is why a whole family can be assembled without opening a single transcript.
